concerns.text: T045 introduces a 'sampled fallback' mechanism allowing the pipeline to proceed with partial data if RAM is exceeded. This silently relaxes FR-001 and Constitution Principle II (Verified Accuracy), which mandate fetching the full canonical dataset or halting. Sampling is not a verified source and degrades the scientific validity of the 2011-2024 time-series analysis.

T016 sets a hard coverage threshold of 50% ('If coverage < 50%, exit with code 1'). This contradicts SC-001 in the spec, which explicitly defers the target threshold to the implementation phase based on statistical power analysis. Hardcoding a 50% threshold in the task without spec authorization is a retroactive narrowing of the acceptance criteria.

T014 mandates calculating 'CNO/p' ratios. While FR-001 requires retrieving CNO data, FR-003 and US-2 only mandate the calculation of He/p and Fe/p ratios. Adding CNO/p to the deliverable scope without a corresponding functional requirement or acceptance criterion in the spec constitutes scope creep and a silent relaxation of the defined analysis boundaries.

T020 requires deriving 'modulation amplitude trends' for absolute fluxes. However, the spec (US-2, FR-006) defines 'modulation amplitude' as the result of a sinusoidal fit (peak-to-trough difference) performed in US-3 (T028). T020 cannot logically derive this trend before the amplitude calculation exists, creating a broken dependency chain that violates the logical flow of the spec's requirements.

T023 is a redundant 'checkpoint' task that claims to save/verify `correlation_results.csv`, which is already the explicit output of T020. This creates a logical conflict where the source of truth for the artifact is ambiguous, violating the Single Source of Truth principle (Constitution Principle IV) regarding artifact generation.

T024 flags non-significant results using a fixed p > 0.01 threshold. SC-002 and US-2 define the significance threshold (p < 0.01) specifically for the 'maximum correlation found', not for every individual lag/point. Applying a strict flag to every point without a multiple-comparison correction (e.,g, Bonferroni) specified in the plan/spec risks generating false positives and misinterpreting the statistical validity.
